name: bench

purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch
purpose.style: normal (upgrade: the same asset, built better)

brief.prompt: a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: thick plank seat on clearly splayed legs with a stretcher, whole bench in frame

turnaround.prompt: orthographic turnaround sheet, front view, side view, back view, evenly spaced, same scale, a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 16:9
turnaround.pick_reason: long side, end view and three-quarter view in one row; the others stacked views in two rows

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: First build to the brief: 1.60 x 0.42 x 0.45 m, 0.12 m two-plank seat, A-frame legs (0.105 to 0.135 m), caps, end rails, stretcher with tenon and peg, small braces. Orthographic hero camera calibrated to -40/16.
Seat top raised to 0.56 m, legs chunkier (0.13 to 0.16 m), wider splay (feet at +-0.27), braces bigger (0.075 m) and longer; recalibrated to -34/12.
Darker walnut and dark timber, crisper bevels, wider seam, longer tenon and bigger peg; harness run for the sheet reference view.
Height swept (0.47 to 0.56 m) and settled at 0.52 m as a compromise with the brief's low bench; feet clamped flat to the ground; hero camera switched to an 85 mm perspective at -38/12.

Stretcher and end rails lowered to 0.17 m and thickened (0.10 m), legs lean 3 cm outward along X, braces from x 0.50 to 0.24; lowering the stretcher further to 0.155 m scored lower and was reverted. Final 768 px / 48 samples render.

what_was_done: A 1.6 m trestle bench with its long side at the front (-Y). The MJ hero sees the left (-X) end and the long front, so it is matched from off the front-left corner (-X, -Y).

The hero wins. views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed by hue (backdrop and cast shadow have G/R about 0.9, the wood is red-brown), keeping the real openings between seat, legs, braces and stretcher. The turnaround sheet drew a taller, lighter bench with thin straight legs, so per the art director it is used for proportions of parts only; its long view (view_front.png) is scored for reference (0.32) and the end and second long views are dropped.

hero_check.py renders from 38 deg off the front towards -X and 12 deg up with an 85 mm perspective lens pulled back to the harness framing (the hero's near end is slightly larger than the far one; orthographic scored 0.02 lower and the harness 50 mm lens 0.06 lower). Calibrated over a yaw/elevation grid, then held fixed.

Plank_Walnut: two 0.203 m planks, 0.12 m thick, 1.60 m long, with a 16 mm seam down the middle; each plank is a slightly different length and its end vertices are pushed and pulled up to 12 mm for rough, chunky sawn ends. 12 mm one-segment bevels.

Plank_Walnut: two A-frame pairs at x = +-0.58 m, splayed from y = +-0.12 at the cap to +-0.27 at the foot and leaning 3 cm outward along X, tapering from 0.13 x 0.10 m at the top to 0.16 x 0.12 m at the foot; feet cut flat to the ground. A 0.13 x 0.44 x 0.065 m cross-rail (cap) under the seat at each end.

Timber_Dark: a low end rail between each leg pair, a 0.075 x 0.10 m stretcher at 0.17 m running through both end rails and out 0.13 m as a through-tenon, a vertical peg through each tenon, and a diagonal brace from the stretcher (x = +-0.50) up to the seat underside (x = +-0.24) at each end.

3 objects, one material each: seat and legs Plank_Walnut, frame Timber_Dark (both timber role). 660 triangles (budget 2k). Origin at the footprint centre on the ground. No animation, export_animations=False.
construction.creative_additions: Rough sawn plank ends of slightly different lengths, and through-tenons with pegs at both ends of the stretcher.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.858 from the calibrated hero camera.
Reads at small size as a heavy slab on two splayed trestles with a dark stretcher and braces: two browns, chunky blocks.
660 triangles, a third of the budget.
off: Seat top is at 0.52 m, not the 0.45 m in the brief: the hero's legs are longer relative to the 1.6 m seat (IoU rose steadily with height: 0.735 at 0.47 m, 0.80 at 0.53 m, 0.82 at 0.56 m), so 0.52 m is a compromise between the hero and a low bench.
The splayed feet make the footprint 0.64 m deep against the 0.42 m seat; the hero's feet stand out past the seat edges, and narrower feet scored lower.
The turnaround sheet view scores 0.32: it drew a taller, lighter bench with thin straight legs, which the art director told us to ignore.
The hero's peg is a lumpy hand-cut block; here it is a plain bevelled block on the tenon end.
No wood grain, cracks or knots: flat colours only, per the game rules.

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
